We transfer the negative into the numerator of the fraction, and proceed with cross-multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{u+2}{3} & =-\frac{3-u}{2} \\ \frac{u+2}{3} & =\frac{-(3-u)}{2} \\ \frac{u+2}{3} & =\frac{-3+u}{2} \\ (u+2)\cdot 2 & =3\cdot (-3+u)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we proceed as usual to solve the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u+2)\cdot 2 & =3\cdot (-3+u) \\ 2u+4 & =-9+3u \\ 2u+4-2u & =-9+3u-2u \\ 4 & =-9+u \\ 4+9 & =-9+u+9 \\ 13 & =u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=13.$
